text:
Let (M, g) and (N, h) be connected, nonempty Riemannian manifolds. Suppose that (M, g) is complete with respect to its Riemannian distance and that pi : M -> N is a local isometry. Then pi is a surjective Riemannian covering map, meaning a smooth covering map that is locally an isometry.

Manifolds are assumed Hausdorff and second-countable. In the cited lecture series, a complete Riemannian manifold is understood to be connected; this is the convention used here.
